set.approach: The summit road (Highway 5) is seasonal and closed in winter, so in the cold months the approach adds a long walk up the road or in from Echo Lake via the Chicago Lakes basin. From the Summit Lake parking area, walk to the east end of the lake and head southwest into the Summit Lake bowl below the north face. The Diamond is a true couloir with rock walls on both sides, hidden behind the large buttress on the west side of the north face. Its neighbours are the broad snowfield to the left and the First Apron to the right. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
set.descent_text: Follow the snow as it steepens up to the cliff band where it stops, then keep left (east) of the steep rock and take a couple of Class 4 steps up to the west ridge. Old tat marks where parties went right; avoid that. The summit is a short Class 2 ridge walk from there. In good snow cover the couloir is also skied back to Summit Lake. Crampons and an axe are the norm, and a rope is optional for the Class 4 ground.

review.notes: MP route page and ski guide agree: couloir behind west buttress, snow ends, Class 3-4 to west ridge, Class 2 to summit. Ridge distance and counts left out.

set.approach: This line is on the Chicago Lakes side, not the Summit Lake bowl. From Echo Lake follow the Chicago Creek trail up to the first Chicago Lake, cross the valley and the lake, and climb to the main rock buttress. The route is on the right side of the buttress, well right of The Road. The summit road above is closed in winter, so the Echo Lake walk-in is the usual way. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
set.descent_text: The route finishes on the ridge above the buttress. Walk east along the ridge to the saddle and drop to the Mount Blue Sky road, then follow the road back down toward Echo Lake. The road is closed to vehicles in winter, and the walk down it is long, so budget daylight and be ready for snow-covered pavement.

review.notes: Concrete Shoes, The Road and Road Less Warren all agree: Chicago Creek trail to first lake, buttress, ridge/col, road, back to Echo Lake. Distances omitted.

Follow that trail back along the rim to the Chicago Lakes overlook, a short walk from the Summit Lake area. Take care on the narrow upper gully and on any cornice or soft snow at the exit. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

The Second Apron is the buttress due west of Summit Lake. From the Summit Lake parking area, cross toward it and climb to the base of the dihedral system at the right side of the apron. Conditions change the character of this route a lot between spring snow and fall rock. These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
set.descent_text: The route ends on a large terrace; cross it to the left and exit by the easiest path to the ridge. To come down, drop into the couloir between the Second and Third Aprons: a short rappel from the top gets you onto steep snow that is then downclimbed. Alternatively walk down one of the main trails along the ridge. Bring crampons and an axe for the snow.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent; area page places the Second Apron due west of the lake. Rappel count not stated so left out.
